change.summary: Both fixed-5120 add+rmsnorm entry points accept the verifier row slab (1 <= rows <= 8) and launch one block per row, and the gfx1100 package declares GGUF_NORM_RESIDUAL_DECODE_POLICIES for (1..8, 5120) under the plain and the UD-preset-extended keys. The kernel and both registry keys already existed but were unreachable on this backend: only gfx1151 declared the policy, and it admitted rows == 1 alone, so every W7900 call fell through to the generic local256 owner - the rows-3 verifier slab and the rows-1 decode alike.
change.arithmetic_neutral_basis: One block owns one row, so blockIdx.x only selects the row base. Every per-thread partial, the reduction tree (three explicit levels at 128/64/32 plus five wave exchanges, which reproduces the generic nine-barrier tree level for level), the rsqrtf argument and the epilogue are unchanged, and the register-cached values are exactly the x+add sums the generic owner recomputes in its second pass.
change.why_the_generic_owner_was_slow: The generic local256 owner has a runtime-trip-count loop over hidden_size and no register cache, so it reloads x and add for its second pass and pays nine tree barriers. The fixed-5120 leaf unrolls both passes, caches the 20 per-thread values in registers, and reduces with two block barriers.

bit_identity.method: Both leaves run against their generic counterparts on real bf16 tensors at hidden_size 5120, rows 1/2/3/4/6/8; norm_out and residual_out compared elementwise.

verifier_census_ab.note: Single-arm sequential runs on the same host and session, baseline measured minutes before the change. The 985 calls/step count is identical in both arms, so no launch was added or removed.

paired_suite.binding_gates: all four arms binding_passed=True timing_evidence_valid=True; true no-MTP AR denominator present, GPU/CPU acceptance agreement, deterministic repeats, faster than true AR; ud arms complete_exact 0/20 divergent
paired_suite.note: The change is bit-identical, so the true-AR movement is a pure speed effect: 127 norm launches per step at 12.0 -> 5.1 us is about -0.9 ms on a 31.3 ms single-row AR step (-2.9%), which matches the measured +2.5-2.7%. The MTP B3 step is roughly twice as long, so the same absolute saving is about half the percentage and sits inside the acceptance-driven spread.

incident.first_attempt: Declaring the policy for both layers without generalising the plain-rmsnorm entry point. The prefill path (_run_linear_attention_prefill_layer_rows -> _run_attention_norm_rows) resolved the rmsnorm leaf for a row count in 2..8 and the C entry rejected it with HIP error 1.
incident.resolution: Both entry points now accept rows 1..8. The policy table is keyed by shape only, so it cannot express 'rows 1-8 for add_rmsnorm but rows 1 for rmsnorm'.

next_lead.note: Separate kernel with no fixed-5120 sibling and no policy table; needs a kRoundSum variant plus a rows-aware resolver at _rounded_add_rmsnorm_fn (qwen35_gguf_runner.py:9079 already knows rows).

numerics_gate.note: Both repeats are identical to the last digit. The bit-identity proof is the stronger statement: the leaves are byte-identical to the owners they replace, so this gate could not move as a result of the change. Its value here is that it is green on the retained default.
